topic: What if you lived on Mars for a year?
title: WHAT IF YOU
LIVED ON MARS FOR A YEAR?

science.claim: Four crew volunteers spent 378 days inside Mars Dune Alpha, entering on 19 October 2025 and stepping out on 31 October 2026.
science.working: CHAPEA Mission 2 habitat simulation duration reported directly by NASA as 378 days from ingress on 19 Oct 2025 to egress on 31 Oct 2026.

science.claim: Mars Dune Alpha is a roughly 1,700-square-foot 3D-printed habitat at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, with zero windows.
science.working: Direct NASA facility specification for CHAPEA's Mars Dune Alpha habitat.

science.claim: Crew members were Ross Elder (commander, test pilot), Ellen Ellis (medical officer), James Spicer (flight engineer), and Matthew Montgomery (science officer).
science.working: CHAPEA Mission 2 crew roster and assigned roles from NASA.

science.claim: Communication delays between the habitat and outside took up to 22 minutes each way.
science.working: Simulated one-way Earth-Mars light-time communication delay up to 22 minutes each way.

science.claim: Crew operations included simulated Marswalks, remotely flying a drone and driving a rover from inside, tracking consumables, hydroponic vegetables, seed-germination experiments in simulated Martian soil vs control, stationary bike exercise, and biological sample collections.
science.working: Operational activities and observations reported by the CHAPEA Mission 2 crew and NASA.

science.claim: While CHAPEA Mission 2 was inside, astronaut Jack Hathaway completed a 237-day mission on the International Space Station, and Artemis II astronauts flew around the Moon and set the record for the farthest humans have travelled from Earth.
science.working: Parallel human spaceflight milestones noted in NASA's CHAPEA Mission 2 reflection article.

science.claim: The first CHAPEA mission ended on 6 July 2024; NASA's Sara Whiting described the data as supporting future Mars crews and Moon Base planning ('the now moment').
science.working: CHAPEA Mission 1 completion date and program context from NASA.
